soil-water-004.q: Why do crop residues and plant cover reduce splash erosion?
soil-water-004.a: They soften the impact of raindrops, whose kinetic energy is what throws soil particles out of the crater each drop makes.

soil-water-043.q: How does a process-based erosion model differ from an empirical one?
soil-water-043.a: A process-based model solves equations for detachment, transport and deposition, while an empirical model relates soil loss statistically to environmental and management factors.

soil-water-095.q: Why are the pale, eroded hilltops in many fields wrongly blamed on water erosion?
soil-water-095.a: They are actually made by tillage erosion, which strips organic-rich topsoil from convex spots.

soil-water-113.q: What left prairie soil open to erosion once settlers plowed it?
soil-water-113.a: Plowing replaced the prairie grasses and their extensive fibrous roots with crops, exposing the topsoil to wind and rain.

soil-water-005.q: What are the two steps of sheet erosion?
soil-water-005.a: Rainsplash first loosens small particles, then a thin, uniform sheet flow carries them a short distance.

soil-water-039.q: Why is a change in soil organic matter an unreliable sign of tillage erosion?
soil-water-039.a: Many other factors also affect organic matter, so a change does not necessarily mean soil was lost.

soil-water-029.q: Why does wind build separate sandy and silty deposits?
soil-water-029.a: Wind sorts sand from silt and clay, laying sand down as ergs and carrying silt further from the source to form loess.

soil-water-064.q: How does heavy rain make a slope more likely to fail?
soil-water-064.a: Pore water pressure on the slip surface lowers effective normal stress and friction, while the added groundwater makes the soil heavier.

soil-water-008.q: How does chemical erosion differ from physical erosion?
soil-water-008.a: Physical erosion removes rock or soil as solid sediment particles, whereas chemical erosion is usually measured from the dissolved load streams carry.

soil-water-049.q: Why can solifluction deposits be used to infer past climates?
soil-water-049.a: Solifluction needs cold, humid conditions, so its deposits show such a climate once prevailed.

soil-water-252.q: A debris flow is as dense as other landslides; why does it flow almost like water?
soil-water-252.a: High pore-fluid pressure liquefies the sediment.

soil-water-031.q: Why do silt fences often give poor results in the field?
soil-water-031.a: Fine particles soon clog the fabric, and fences are often badly placed, installed or maintained.

soil-water-062.q: Why do shallow landslides often occur where permeable soil lies over less permeable soil?
soil-water-062.a: The lower layer traps water, pressure builds, and the saturated topsoil slides off.

soil-water-076.q: Which agency did the Soil Erosion Service become, and who led it?
soil-water-076.a: Hugh Hammond Bennett led it; it became the Soil Conservation Service, now the NRCS.

soil-water-101.q: What is one of the best defences against earthflows?
soil-water-101.a: Draining slopes, since saturated clay, fine sand and silt begin to flow and more water means faster flow.

soil-water-052.q: Why are anionic rather than cationic flocculants best practice in open systems?
soil-water-052.a: Cationic flocculants such as chitosan can cause hypoxia in fish.

soil-water-066.q: How does vegetation help stabilize a slope with shallow landslides?
soil-water-066.a: Roots reinforce the upper soil, and interception and transpiration dry it.

soil-water-108.q: Why does harvesting trees on a slope raise the risk of sloughing and slope failure?
soil-water-108.a: Roots hold the surface, and losing their strength can lower the safety factor so far that a moderate storm brings failure.

soil-water-250.q: Why is a desert pavement taken as a sign of a surface's relative age?

soil-water-257.q: When might gabions be chosen over riprap to protect a bank?
soil-water-257.a: On steep banks where the flow is too fast for riprap.

soil-water-124.q: What separates a marsh from a swamp?
soil-water-124.a: A marsh has herbaceous plants, while a swamp has woody plants.

soil-water-129.q: How do marsh plants cope with wet mud low in oxygen?
soil-water-129.a: Many have aerenchyma that carry air down to their roots.

soil-water-121.q: Why does peat accumulate in bogs even though plant growth there is slow?
soil-water-121.a: Decay is slower still in the oxygen-poor, saturated bog soil.

soil-water-147.q: What makes minerotrophic water neutral or alkaline?
soil-water-147.a: Dissolved bases such as calcium or magnesium ions make it base-rich.

soil-water-126.q: What keeps the pH of a rich fen relatively stable?
soil-water-126.a: Bicarbonate from calcium carbonate that groundwater dissolves as it passes limestone buffers the pH.
